claims.text: The two-phase LLM framework achieved an F1-score of 0.983 with semantic matching and 0.968 with binary overlap on the full dataset of 700 patient notes.
The two-phase LLM framework achieved an F1-score of 0.973 with semantic matching and 0.952 with binary overlap using a few-shot subset of 100 patient notes.
The framework reduced hallucinated features by 89.9% from 3081 to 311 features on the private dataset compared to the vanilla LLM baseline.
The framework reduced missing features by 88.9% from 6376 to 708 features on the private dataset compared to the vanilla LLM baseline.
Expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147 across five training epochs during few-shot training.
The Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036 across training epochs.
The framework combines instructing fine-tuning with confidence-regularization fine-tuning using bidirectional semantic mapping penalties.

evidence.description: Our framework achieved state-of-the-art performance with F1=0.983 (semantic matching) and F1=0.968 (binary overlap) on the entire dataset.
Maintained high performance with F1=0.973 (semantic matching) and F1=0.952 (binary overlap) while using only 100 of 700 patient notes.
It reduced hallucinations by 89.9% (from 3081 to 311 features)... on the private dataset compared with the baseline LLM with few-shot in-context learning.
And missing features by 88.9% (from 6376 to 708) on the private dataset compared with the baseline LLM with few-shot in-context learning.
Calibration evaluation on few-shot training (100 patient notes) showed that the expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147.
Whereas the Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036.

Our two-phase training approach: instructing fine-tuning and confidence-regularization fine-tuning with loss functions penalizing overconfident incorrect predictions captured using bidirectional matching targeting hallucination and missing features.

methodologies.name: Two-Phase LLM Fine-Tuning Framework
methodologies.description: A two-phase framework combining instructing fine-tuning for extraction guidance with confidence-regularization fine-tuning using bidirectional semantic matching penalties to reduce hallucinated and missing clinical features.
datasets: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) Step-2 Clinical Skills dataset
conditions: Inference matching gate with regex, TF-IDF, and sentence embedding similarity

limitations.text: The framework exhibits an increased expected calibration error (ECE from 0.060 to 0.147), producing stable conservative confidence estimates that become underconfident as accuracy increases.
The framework was evaluated on USMLE Step-2 Clinical Skills examination notes but lacks evaluation on unstructured or multilingual clinical records.
The validation pipeline requires predefined target feature lists to perform matching gate and cosine similarity checks, limiting direct applicability to open-ended extraction tasks.
The evaluation did not systematically test performance across alternative open-source model backbones such as Llama-3-Instruct or Mistral-7B-Instruct.
Prior BERT-based and statistical NLP approaches require extensive span-level annotation and exhibit limited ability to capture contextual semantic variability in complex clinical language.

future_work.text: Investigate bidirectional generation, encoder-decoder architectures, and matching-based retrieval models to improve token-level positional grounding in span-sensitive tasks.
Perform domain-specific continual pretraining on clinical corpora such as MIMIC-III to enhance understanding of medical terminologies.
Evaluate the framework on unstructured electronic health records, radiology reports, and multilingual patient records.
Systematically investigate parameter sensitivity for confidence regularization across different clinical NLP domains and LLM backbones.
